---
title: "Template: Textures from Scratch"
description: The complete asset path for retexturing and adding art in neoLegacy — terrain.png/items.png atlas editing, mob/armor textures in Common/res, the RebuildArc UI workflow, and the folder-pack alternative, with verification steps.
---

This is a **complete, top-to-bottom recipe** for changing what neoLegacy draws:
recolour an existing block, add a brand-new block texture, retexture a mob, edit
armor, and (for a UI reskin) rebuild the `.arc`. Unlike PC Minecraft, neoLegacy
does **not** stitch its atlas from loose PNGs at runtime — 4J replaced that with a
build-time hardcoded UV map. That one fact changes everything about how you add
art, so we start there.

For the reference-level anatomy of the pipeline (the codegen chain, the `.arc`
format spec, the `colours.xml` biome override), read
[Textures & Asset Pipeline](/slop-docs/modding/textures-assets/) and
[Texture Packs & Resources](/slop-docs/client/resources/) alongside this page.
For consuming a new texture from a new block, see
[Adding Blocks](/slop-docs/modding/adding-blocks/).

## 0. How texturing actually works here (read this first)

Three separate systems draw everything on screen, and each is edited differently:

| System | What it covers | Source files | How you edit it |
|--------|----------------|--------------|-----------------|
| **Pre-stitched atlas** | All blocks + all items | `Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/terrain.png`, `items.png` | Edit the atlas PNG at a fixed grid slot |
| **Loose per-file textures** | Mobs, armor, GUI, environment, particles, sun/moon | `Common/res/mob/*.png`, `armor/*.png`, `gui/*.png`, … | Edit the single PNG directly |
| **Animated block strips** | fire, lava, water, portal, prismarine, sea_lantern | `Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/textures/blocks/*.png` + `*.txt` | Edit the vertical strip + its frame list |

The atlas UV coordinates are **hardcoded in C++** in `PreStitchedTextureMap::loadUVs()`
(`Minecraft.Client/PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:322`). At startup `Textures::Textures()`
builds two maps (`Textures.cpp:313`):

```cpp
terrain = new PreStitchedTextureMap(Icon::TYPE_TERRAIN, L"terrain", L"textures/blocks/", missingNo, true);
items   = new PreStitchedTextureMap(Icon::TYPE_ITEM,    L"items",   L"textures/items/",  missingNo, true);
```

`Icon::TYPE_TERRAIN = 0`, `Icon::TYPE_ITEM = 1` (`Minecraft.World/Icon.h:8`). Each
map loads its master image (`terrain.png` / `items.png`) then hands out named
`SimpleIcon` sub-rectangles into that image based on the hardcoded row/column table.
Blocks and items look up their icon **by name** — e.g. `Tile::stone` is registered
with `->setIconName(L"stone")` (`Minecraft.World/Tile.cpp:378`), and the name
`L"stone"` maps to atlas slot `(row 0, column 1)` in `loadUVs()`. If you move a
texture's pixels but not its slot, or add a name with no slot, you get the
`missingno` magenta/black checkerboard.

> The `.arc` archive (`MediaWindows64.arc`) does **not** contain terrain or mob
> textures — it holds the Scaleform/Iggy **UI movies** (`.swf`). You only touch it
> for a menu/HUD reskin (§7). Block/item/mob art all lives loose under `Common/res`.

## 1. The terrain atlas grid — slot math

`terrain.png` is a **16-column** grid. Crucially it is **not** 16 rows — the
terrain map uses `vertRatio = 1.0f/32.0f` (`PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:673`) while
`horizRatio = 1.0f/16.0f` (line 672). So each cell is `1/16` of the width and
`1/32` of the height: a **16-wide, 32-tall** cell grid. The shipped `terrain.png`
uses rows 0 through 26, so at a 16-px tile size the file is **256 px wide × 512 px
tall** (16×32 cells). Items is the simpler case: `items.png` uses `1/16 × 1/16`
(`PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:340-341`), a **16×16** grid, **256 × 256 px**.

The UV rectangle for a cell is generated by the `ADD_ICON(row, column, name)` macro
(`PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:318`):

```cpp
#define ADD_ICON(row, column, name) \
  (texturesByName[name] = new SimpleIcon(name, name, \
     horizRatio*column, vertRatio*row, \
     horizRatio*(column+1), vertRatio*(row+1)));
```

So to convert a slot to **pixel coordinates** in the PNG (with a tile size `T`,
16 px by default):

```
x0 = column * T
y0 = row    * T          (row uses the /32 grid, but pixel rows are still row*T
x1 = x0 + T               because T = height/32 = width/16)
y1 = y0 + T
```

A few real slots from `loadUVs()` you can use as landmarks:

| Name | Row | Col | Pixel top-left (16-px) | Source line |
|------|-----|-----|------------------------|-------------|
| `grass_top` | 0 | 0 | (0, 0) | `PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:675` |
| `stone` | 0 | 1 | (16, 0) | `:677` |
| `dirt` | 0 | 2 | (32, 0) | `:678` |
| `cobblestone` | 1 | 0 | (0, 16) | `:694` |
| `gold_ore` | 2 | 0 | (0, 32) | `:711` |
| `diamond_ore` | 3 | 2 | (32, 48) | `:730` |
| `coal_block` | 16 | 0 | (0, 256) | `:943` |
| `sea_lantern` | 23 | 13 | (208, 368) | `:1058` |

Two icons in the terrain map span **2×2 cells** via `ADD_ICON_SIZE(row,col,name,h,w)`:
`water_flow` at `(12,14)` size 2×2 (`:895`) and `lava_flow` at `(14,14)` size 2×2
(`:926`). Give those a 32×32 px region, not 16×16.

## 2. Recipe A — recolour an existing block

Goal: make **stone** purple. Stone's icon is slot `(row 0, col 1)`, pixels
`(16,0)–(32,16)`.

1. **Locate the source atlas.** The master image the game actually loads is:

   ```
   Minecraft.Client/Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/terrain.png
   ```

   (`DefaultTexturePack::getResourceImplementation()` resolves the drive to
   `Common\res\TitleUpdate\res` on Windows64 — `DefaultTexturePack.cpp:100`.) A
   second, smaller `terrain.png` sits loose at `Common/res/terrain.png` (~65 KB) —
   that is the legacy 1.2.2-era copy and is **not** what the default pack loads. The
   one the game actually stitches is the ~216 KB file under `TitleUpdate/res/`.
   **Edit that one.**

2. **Open it in an editor that preserves the alpha channel and does no resampling**
   (GIMP, Aseprite, Paint.NET, Photoshop). Turn OFF any auto-anti-aliasing —
   neoLegacy samples with `TFLT_NEAREST` (`PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:85-86`), so
   every pixel is displayed 1:1 and blurred edges will look wrong.

3. **Paint only inside the 16×16 cell at (16,0)–(32,16).** Do not resize the canvas.

4. **Regenerate the mipmaps (or delete the pre-baked ones).** See §5 — if you leave
   the stale `terrainMipMapLevel2.png` / `terrainMipMapLevel3.png` in place they
   will still show the old stone colour at distance.

5. Rebuild the client (§6) and verify (§8).

That is the entire flow for recolouring any existing block or item — find its
`setIconName` in `Minecraft.World/Tile.cpp`, find that name in `loadUVs()`, edit
those pixels.

## 3. Recipe B — add a NEW block texture to a free slot

Goal: give a new block (say one you added following
[Adding Blocks](/slop-docs/modding/adding-blocks/)) its own atlas cell.

The terrain map has unused cells. Scanning `loadUVs()` (`PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:670`
onward) shows rows 20–26 are sparsely populated — e.g. row 20 only defines columns
0–15 partially (`flower_tulip_orange` at col 5, `log_acacia` at col 8, …). Pick a
genuinely empty `(row,col)` — the safest is a fresh high row. Here we use `(25,5)`.

1. **Paint your 16×16 tile** into `terrain.png` at pixels `(5*16, 25*16) = (80, 400)`.
   If the shipped `terrain.png` is shorter than 26 rows tall, extend the canvas
   height to at least `(25+1)*16 = 416` px (keep width 256) and fill the new area
   with transparent pixels before painting your cell.

2. **Register the UV slot in code.** Add one line in `loadUVs()` inside the
   `else` (terrain) branch, next to the other row-25 entries near
   `PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:1088`:

   ```cpp
   ADD_ICON(25, 5, L"myblock");
   ```

3. **Point your Tile at it.** In `Minecraft.World/Tile.cpp` where you construct the
   tile, chain `->setIconName(L"myblock")`, matching the existing pattern
   (`Tile.cpp:378`):

   ```cpp
   Tile::myBlock = (new Tile(NEW_ID, Material::stone))
       ->setDestroyTime(1.5f)
       ->setSoundType(Tile::SOUND_STONE)
       ->setIconName(L"myblock")
       ->setDescriptionId(IDS_TILE_MYBLOCK);
   ```

   At stitch time, `PreStitchedTextureMap::stitch()` walks every tile and calls
   `tile->registerIcons(this)` (`PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:49-55`); that resolves
   `L"myblock"` against `texturesByName` via `registerIcon()` (`:280`). A name with
   no matching `ADD_ICON` returns `missingPosition` (the magenta `missingno`), which
   is your signal that step 2 was skipped.

4. **Mipmaps + rebuild** as in §5–§6.

> **Different faces:** blocks that use distinct top/side/bottom textures override
> `getTexture(int face, int data)` / `registerIcons()` in their Tile subclass and
> register several names (grep for `grass_top`/`grass_side`/`grass_side_overlay`,
> all three registered separately). Follow whichever existing Tile most resembles
> yours.

## 4. Recipe C — animated block textures (fire, lava, water, …)

Animated block textures are the **one** part of the terrain path that is NOT baked
into `terrain.png`. They live as vertical frame strips under:

```
Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/textures/blocks/
```

The shipped set is `fire_0`, `fire_1`, `lava`, `lava_flow`, `portal`,
`prismarine`, `sea_lantern`, `water`, `water_flow` — each a `.png` strip plus a
`.txt` frame descriptor. `PreStitchedTextureMap::makeTextureAnimated()`
(`PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:201`) loads the strip and, if the pack returns a
non-empty animation string, drives the frames.

**The `.txt` format** (parsed by `AbstractTexturePack::getAnimationString()`,
`AbstractTexturePack.cpp:287`): one frame index per line, top-to-bottom. Two forms:

- `fire_0.txt` — plain indices: `8`, `9`, `10`, … `7,` (a comma is tolerated). Each
  number picks the Nth 16×16 frame down the strip.
- `lava.txt` — `frame*ticks` form: `0*2`, `1*2`, … means "show frame 0 for 2 ticks,
  frame 1 for 2 ticks". The strip then ping-pongs back down (`18*2`, `17*2`, …).

To make a **new animated block texture**:

1. Create `Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/textures/blocks/myanim.png` — a vertical strip
   of `N` stacked 16×16 frames (so `16 × 16N` px).
2. Create `myanim.txt` listing the play order, one `frame` or `frame*ticks` per line.
3. Register a **placeholder slot** for it in `terrain.png`/`loadUVs()` the same way
   as §3 (the atlas holds the *first* frame / a static fallback, and the animated
   texture overwrites that region each tick — see `stitch()` copying `preStitched`
   rects then `makeTextureAnimated`). Point your tile's `setIconName(L"myanim")`.

`PreStitchedTextureMap::cycleAnimationFrames()` (`:263`) is what ticks them; it is
driven from the render/update loop.

## 5. Mipmaps — the gotcha that shows stale textures at distance

Terrain and items are created with `mipmap = true` (the trailing `true` in the
`new PreStitchedTextureMap(...)` calls, `Textures.cpp:313-314`). At upload time
`Textures::getTexture(...)` (`Textures.cpp:683`) builds each mip level. For each
level it **prefers a pre-baked mip PNG if one exists**, else it generates the level
by 2×2 box-filtering (`Texture::crispBlend`) the level above (`Textures.cpp:810-853`).

Pre-baked mip files are named `<basename>MipMapLevel<L+1>.png`
(`BufferedImage.cpp:150-159`) — i.e. level 1 → `MipMapLevel2`, level 2 →
`MipMapLevel3`. The shipped tree includes:

```
Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/terrainMipMapLevel2.png   (128×256)
Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/terrainMipMapLevel3.png   (64×128)
```

**Consequence:** if you edit `terrain.png` but leave those two files, the game keeps
showing the *old* pixels once a surface is more than a few blocks away. You have two
options:

- **Simplest:** delete `terrainMipMapLevel2.png` and `terrainMipMapLevel3.png`. The
  engine will then auto-generate correct mips from your edited `terrain.png` via
  `crispBlend`. Slightly softer than hand-tuned mips but always correct.
- **Precise:** regenerate them. Downscale your edited `terrain.png` by 2× into
  `terrainMipMapLevel2.png` and by 4× into `terrainMipMapLevel3.png`, using
  **box/area** downsampling (not bicubic), matching the engine's box filter.

`items.png` ships without pre-baked mip PNGs, so item edits auto-mip with no extra
step. Sun/moon/clouds/shadow are explicitly excluded from mipmapping
(`Textures.cpp:628-632`) — no mip files needed there.

## 6. Recipe D — retexture a mob or armor (loose PNGs)

Mobs and armor are the easy case: one PNG per texture, no atlas, no slot math.

**Mobs.** Each mob renderer returns a `ResourceLocation` built from a `TN_*` enum,
and `Textures::preLoaded[]` (`Textures.cpp:27`) maps that enum ordinal to a relative
path. Examples straight from the table:

| `TN_*` enum | Path (under `res/`) | File on disk | Renderer |
|-------------|---------------------|--------------|----------|
| `TN_MOB_CREEPER` | `mob/creeper` | `Common/res/mob/creeper.png` | `CreeperRenderer.cpp:8` |
| `TN_MOB_ZOMBIE` | `mob/zombie` | `Common/res/mob/zombie.png` | `ZombieRenderer.cpp:8` |
| `TN_POWERED_CREEPER` | `armor/power` | `Common/res/armor/power.png` | `CreeperRenderer.cpp:7` |
| `TN_MOB_PIGZOMBIE` | `mob/pigzombie` | `Common/res/mob/pigzombie.png` | `ZombieRenderer.cpp:7` |

So `CreeperRenderer::getTextureLocation()` returns `&CREEPER_LOCATION`
(`CreeperRenderer.cpp:95`), which is `ResourceLocation(TN_MOB_CREEPER)` → `mob/creeper`
→ the file `Common/res/mob/creeper.png`. To retexture the creeper: **edit that PNG in
place.** No code change. Keep the same dimensions (64×32 for classic mob layouts).

There are two copies to be aware of, same as terrain: the live one is under
`Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/mob/` where present (e.g. `mob/zombie.png`,
`mob/villager/…`, `mob/enderdragon/…`), with `Common/res/mob/` as the older base.
When both exist, the `TitleUpdate/res` copy is what `DefaultTexturePack` resolves.
Edit that one; if only the base `Common/res/mob/` copy exists, edit that.

**Armor.** Armor overlays live in `Common/res/armor/` (and
`Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/armor/`): `<material>_1.png` is the body/legs layer and
`<material>_2.png` is the leggings layer — `cloth_1.png`/`cloth_2.png`,
`iron_1.png`/`iron_2.png`, `diamond_1.png`/`diamond_2.png`, `gold_1.png`,
`chain_1.png`, plus enchant-glow `power.png`. `HumanoidArmorLayer`
consumes them via `AbstractArmorLayer::getArmorModel(slot)`; see
[Entity Rendering](/slop-docs/client/entity-rendering/) for how the layers stack.
To recolour iron armor, edit `iron_1.png` and `iron_2.png` — no code change.

**Player skins.** `char.png`/`char1..7.png` (Steve) and `alex.png`/`alex1..7.png`
(slim) live in `Common/res/mob/` and are enumerated in `preLoaded[]`
(`Textures.cpp:67-82`). These feed the skin-select carousel — see
[Skin Select / Settings](/slop-docs/client/settings/).

## 7. Recipe E — UI / HUD reskin via RebuildArc (the `.arc` workflow)

Everything above covers world/entity art. The **menus, HUD, inventory, logo** are
Scaleform/Iggy movies packed in an `.arc` archive, not PNGs in `res/`. You only need
this section for a UI reskin.

**Where the `.arc` lives.** It is built from the loose media folder
`Common/Media/MediaWindows64/` and copied next to the exe as `MediaWindows64.arc`
during the build (the server targets copy `Common/Media/MediaWindows64.arc`
explicitly; the client resolves it via `app.getArchiveFile(...)`, e.g.
`DefaultTexturePack.cpp:30`). The archive is Java `DataOutputStream` format:
big-endian ints, modified-UTF-8 names, `*`-prefix on a name = zlib-compressed entry.

**The tools** (`tools/`, all Java — compile with `javac`, run with `java`):

| Tool | What it does | Usage |
|------|--------------|-------|
| `ListArc.java` | Print entries (filters to logo/skin/Menu/platform names) | `java ListArc MediaWindows64.arc` |
| `ExtractFromArc.java` | Pull one entry out to a file | `java ExtractFromArc MediaWindows64.arc <name> out.swf` |
| `RebuildArc.java` | Swap updated `.swf`s back in, overwriting the `.arc` in place | `java RebuildArc MediaWindows64.arc <media_dir> [file1.swf …]` |

**End-to-end UI reskin:**

1. **List** the archive to find the movie you want to change:

   ```
   javac tools/ListArc.java
   java -cp tools ListArc build/windows64/Minecraft.Client/Debug/MediaWindows64.arc
   ```

2. **Extract** it:

   ```
   javac tools/ExtractFromArc.java
   java -cp tools ExtractFromArc <path>/MediaWindows64.arc SomeMenu.swf /tmp/SomeMenu.swf
   ```

3. **Edit the SWF.** Open it in JPEXS FFDec (the `tools/*.java` SWF patchers use
   `com.jpexs.decompiler.flash.*`). For simple graphic swaps you replace bitmap
   tags; for logic you edit ActionScript/ABC. neoLegacy ships worked examples of
   both: `ReplaceLogo.java` / `ShiftLogo.java` (logo art) and `PatchHudABC.java`
   (adds hardcore-hearts logic to the Hud class). Save the edited `.swf` into a
   working `media_dir`.

4. **Rebuild** the archive, swapping your `.swf` in:

   ```
   javac tools/RebuildArc.java
   java -cp tools RebuildArc <path>/MediaWindows64.arc /tmp/mymedia SomeMenu.swf
   ```

   `RebuildArc` keeps all other entries byte-identical, marks replaced files as
   uncompressed (`compressed.set(i, false)`, `RebuildArc.java:96`), recomputes the
   offset table, and overwrites the `.arc` in place. Passing no filenames replaces
   **every** `.swf` it finds by name in `media_dir` (`RebuildArc.java:80-85`).

> Because `RebuildArc` overwrites in place, work on the copy in your **build output**
> dir (or back up the source `.arc` first). Re-running the client build will
> regenerate/re-copy the `.arc` from `Common/Media`, wiping your hand-patched one —
> so either re-run `RebuildArc` after each build, or patch the source movies under
> `Common/Media/MediaWindows64/` and let the build repack them.

## 8. Build & test checklist

Textures are copied to the build output as ordinary assets — `.png` is **not** in
the asset-copy exclusion list (`cmake/CopyAssets.cmake:5-16` excludes `.cpp/.h`,
`.xml`, audio, `.xui`, etc., but not images). So a texture-only edit still needs a
build so the copy step runs, and a code-slot edit (§3) needs a recompile.

1. **Build the client** (from [Building neoLegacy](/slop-docs/overview/building/)):

   ```
   cmake --preset windows64
   cmake --build --preset windows64-release --target Minecraft.Client
   ```

   or Linux cross: `./build-linux.sh . Release`.

2. **Run from the output dir** so relative asset paths resolve:

   ```
   build/windows64/Minecraft.Client/Release/Minecraft.Client.exe
   ```

3. **Inspect the stitched result.** `stitch()` writes the assembled atlas to disk
   for debugging: `debug.stitched_terrain.png` and `debug.stitched_items.png`
   (`PreStitchedTextureMap.cpp:157`), dropped in the working directory. Open these to
   confirm your pixels landed in the right cell **before** hunting in-game.

4. **Verify by symptom:**
   - **Magenta/black `missingno` checkerboard** on your block → the icon name has no
     `ADD_ICON` slot (§3 step 2 missing), or the tile's `setIconName` string doesn't
     match. Grep both for the exact wide-string.
   - **Old texture at distance, new up close** → stale
     `terrainMipMapLevel2/3.png` (§5). Delete or regenerate them.
   - **Blurry / bleeding edges** → your editor anti-aliased the cell; repaint with
     nearest-neighbour tools, no feathering.
   - **Whole atlas shifted** → you resized the canvas or changed tile size; every
     slot is computed as `col/16 × row/32`, so the file must stay a clean 16-wide
     grid at a consistent tile size.
   - **Mob texture unchanged** → you edited the base `Common/res/mob/…` copy but a
     `Common/res/TitleUpdate/res/mob/…` copy exists and wins. Edit that one.

## 9. The in-game texture-pack folder alternative (and why it's limited)

PC Minecraft loads loose folders as texture packs at runtime via `FolderTexturePack`
(`FolderTexturePack.cpp`). neoLegacy **has** the class, but the repository scan loop
that would discover user folders is **compiled out**: `TexturePackRepository::updateList()`
is entirely inside an `#if 0 … #endif` block (`TexturePackRepository.cpp:159-218`),
and the dummy-pack registration is also commented (`:43-44`). The live list is just
`DEFAULT_TEXTURE_PACK` (pushed at `:26`). On the console/Windows64 build the
authoritative custom-texture route is the **DLC pack** system
(`DLCTexturePack` / `Common/DLC/`), not a drop-in folder.

So for a **modder**, the practical, supported workflow is exactly §2–§6: **edit the
files under `Common/res` and rebuild.** The `FolderTexturePack` path is present but
not wired for general folder scanning today — treat it as inactive rather than as a
hot-reload mechanism. `FolderTexturePack::getResourceImplementation()` still resolves
against `Common\DummyTexturePack\res` (`FolderTexturePack.cpp:29-32`), and
`Common/DummyTexturePack/res` ships holding only a placeholder (`TFSHOLDER.txt`),
confirming it is a stub.

If you specifically want a swappable pack without recompiling, the honest options are:

- Package your edited `res/` tree as a **DLC pack** (`DLCTexturePack`, feeds off a
  `DLCPack` in `Common/DLC/`) — this is the console-native custom-content path.
- Or maintain your edits as a patch you re-apply to `Common/res` and rebuild.
